messages:
Taylor: odd one from onboarding atlas-48k (int4). Repro shows deterministic token shift around 41k with clear KV eviction events logged just before the drift. float32 baseline clean.
Ibrahim: eviction? we don't GC during prefill normally. which GC mode and what timing?
Taylor: GC mode=aggressive-ttl (we enabled to save mem on the bringup infra). repro: `./tools/long_prefill --model atlas-48k --quant int4 --context 48000 --gc-mode aggressive-ttl --seed 9001 --prefetch-window 8192`
Taylor: log excerpt:
```
[03:41:10] kv: evict key=0x8ff1 abs_pos=40768 ttl_expired=true
[03:41:10] prefetch apply shard=2 id=0x2a10 req=0x99aa abs_pos=40770
[03:41:11] token-check expected=token_40771 actual=token_40770
```
Keiko: hmm int4Metadata packs the abs_pos and ttl tighter, and the GC TTL rounding is in wallclock seconds; maybe under quant kernels the encode path is faster so entries appear older when GC checks run?
Ibrahim: that would be odd but possible: compressed metadata reduces stored timestamp granularity (we pack to 16bits for space) and aggressive-ttl uses a coarse epoch counter; under faster encode loops the relative age computation overflows bucket boundaries.
Taylor: I repro'd locally: turn off aggressive-ttl and drift disappears. `--gc-mode conservative` is clean. With aggressive-ttl we always see eviction ~2 tokens before drift point.
Keiko: could also be interaction with async prefetch: prefetch writes entries with a future abs_pos, but GC compares stored timestamp vs now and treats future-tagged entries as stale if packed sign bit mishandled. Any evidence of negative ages?
Taylor: yes found lines like `kv: computed_age=-3 buckets=65536` right before evict. so sign wrap in packed age field. snippet:
```
[03:40:59] kv: write key=0x8ff1 abs_pos=40768 meta_ts=0xfff5
[03:41:00] kv: computed_age=-3 (wrap)
[03:41:00] kv: evict key=0x8ff1 reason=age_wrap
```
Ibrahim: packing overflow then. Under int4 kernel we write meta_ts with truncated epoch (16-bit), but runtime increments epoch quicker for small quant chunking so wrap happens mid-run. float32 slower so no wrap.
Keiko: solid root-cause. quick mitigations: 1) bump packed epoch width to 32-bit in aggressive-ttl (hotfix) 2) add a guard: never evict keys whose abs_pos > current_token - safety_margin (safety_margin=128 tokens) 3) fix pack/unpack math to use unsigned arithmetic and explicit saturating subtraction to avoid negative ages.
Taylor: plan of action: a) run small repro to confirm patch (Keiko will PR for saturating subtract + safety_margin) b) hotfix bump for aggressive-ttl metadata layout (ops awareness) c) canary on dedicated (ops: request 3 GPUs for 90m) d) run onboarding matrix across gc-mode {aggressive-ttl,conservative} quant {int4,float32} kernel {vector,scalar}
Ibrahim: I'll to run a bisect on the commit that introduced 16-bit packing for meta_ts — original change to reduce memory usage. If we can repro reliably we should revert or make layout conditional on gc-mode.

ops-bot: reserving 3xA100 for team-ml on 2024-11-20T04:00Z-2024-11-20T05:30Z for canary. ticket OP-8055 created.
Keiko: opened PR draft: "kv: saturating-age-check + safety-margin for aggressive-ttl". I'll run unit tests and then the small matrix.
Taylor: uploaded artifacts to s3://redwood-eval/atlas_prefill/1955556666.tar.gz (logs, kv-dumps, small repro script). tracking INF-1777.
Ibrahim: nice find. once patched we should run a sweep across other models to ensure no regressions from changing epoch width.
Keiko: agreed. adding to PR checklist: [ ] unit tests for pack/unpack [ ] matrix runs [ ] canary results [ ] revert plan if mem budget issues.
Taylor: thanks all. will update INF-1777 with triage summary once matrix completes. :rocket:
